- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > 85), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak or use 3-period moving average.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong downward momentum, model frequently fails to correct; apply mean reversion to 10-day average if price drops >5% from prior peak.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often misses early downward turns; adjust by adding 1–2 days of lagged sentiment decay to forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to overfit recent highs; use sentiment-weighted average of 3–5 prior days to anchor forecast.
- If true outcome is below 70, model often ignores sentiment shift; force downward correction if sentiment drops below 0.20 and price >75.
